chunks: Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام.
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Allah does not call you to account for vain speech in your oaths."
He عليه السلام said: "It is: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'"

key_terms.أَبُو بَصِيرٍ: Abu Basir, the narrator transmitting this report
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.ٱللَّغْوِ: vain or unintentional speech not meant as a binding oath

ai.seo_question: What does 'vain speech in your oaths' mean in Qur'an 2:225?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic phrase about unintentional or vain oaths as referring to common expressions spoken habitually, such as saying, 'No, by Allah' or 'Yes, by Allah.' It clarifies that such casual speech does not incur liability as deliberate sworn oaths do.
